Meteoroloji Genel Müdürlüğü (MGM) ile İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediyesi (İBB) Afet Koordinasyon Merkezi (AKOM), yeni haftada etkili olacak sağanak yağış ve fırtınaya ilişkin son tahminlerini yayımladı.
Meteoroloji'nin değerlendirmelerine göre, bugün Kuzey Ege, İç Anadolu'nun kuzey ve doğusu, Batı Karadeniz'in iç kesimleri, Orta ve Doğu Karadeniz, Doğu Anadolu'nun kuzey ve batısı ile İskenderun Körfezi ve Sinop çevrelerinde sağanak ve yer yer gök gürültülü sağanak yağış bekleniyor.
DOĞU KARADENİZ'DE KUVVETLİ SAĞANAK, KIYILARDA KUVVETLİ RÜZGAR
Sağanak yağışların özellikle Doğu Karadeniz kıyılarında yerel olarak kuvvetli olacağı tahmin ediliyor. Rüzgarın ise Marmara ve Kuzey Ege'de kuzeydoğudan, Orta ve Doğu Karadeniz kıyılarında ise kuzeybatıdan saatte 40 ila 60 kilometre hıza ulaşarak kuvvetli esmesi bekleniyor. Gece ve sabah saatlerinde iç ve doğu bölgelerde pus ve yer yer sis görüleceği bildirildi.
İSTANBUL'DA SALI GÖK GÜRÜLTÜLÜ SAĞANAK, ÇARŞAMBA LODOS FIRTINASI
AKOM'un haftalık hava tahmin raporuna göre, İstanbul'da sağanak yağış ve lodos fırtınası peş peşe etkili olacak:
Salı günü gök gürültülü sağanak: Pazartesi günü parçalı bulutlu ve 15 derece civarında seyredecek hava, salı günü yerini gök gürültülü sağanak yağışa bırakacak (16 derece).
Çarşambadan itibaren fırtına şiddetinde lodos: Hafta ortasından itibaren güneyli yönlerden esecek lodosun zaman zaman fırtına şiddetine ulaşması bekleniyor. Lodosla birlikte sıcaklıklar çarşamba günü 18 dereceye, perşembe ve cuma günleri ise 19-20 dereceye kadar yükselecek.
Cumartesi yeniden yağış: Lodos fırtınasının ardından cumartesi günü İstanbul'da yeniden sağanak yağış görüleceği ve sıcaklığın 18 derece civarında seyredeceği tahmin ediliyor.
Meteoroloji'nin haftalık tahminlerine göre, yeni hafta boyunca yurdun farklı bölgelerinde sağanak yağış geçişleri devam edecek. Hava sıcaklıklarının kuzey ve iç kesimlerde bir miktar azalarak mevsim normalleri civarında seyredeceği öngörülürken, yağışların Doğu Karadeniz'in yüksek kesimleri ile Doğu Anadolu'nun kuzeyinde kar şeklinde görülmesi bekleniyor.

An interactive reproduction of a self portrait by Kyffin Williams will allow visitors to feel the texture of the thick oil he used in his paintings
For the first time, the paintings of Sir Kyffin Williams have been brought to life in a new immersive experience at the National Library of Wales.
Technology similar to that used for exhibitions of Van Gogh, Cézanne and LS Lowry will immerse visitors in the mountain landscapes, hillfarms and stormy seas created by the painter, who is considered the defining Welsh artist of the 20th Century.
Images from Williams's oil paintings such as the hill farmer and sheepdog are animated in a 360-degree centrepiece and Sir Kyffin's life story is narrated by Sir Bryn Terfel in a bilingual presentation, with original paintings illuminated on the walls.
The National Library, which received grants of £500,000 to fund the project, said it hoped it will introduce a new audience to Sir Kyffin's work.
There are also interactive installations including a recreation of a self-portrait which can be touched, giving visitors a sense of the texture of Sir Kyffin's oil paintings.
He painted using an impasto technique - where paint is applied so thickly on to a canvas that it stands out in three dimensions.
Sir Kyffin, who was born on Anglesey in 1918, had a long relationship with the National Library, in Aberystwyth, Ceredigion, which has about 2,000 pieces of his work in its collection.
Moving images taken from Sir Kyffin's paintings are projected on to walls in what used to be an office in the national library
In 1950 the library bought its first two pieces from the young artist soon after he left the Slade School of Fine Art in London.
Morfudd Bevan, art curator at the National Library of Wales, said the library paid £15 for an oil painting of Cader Idris and £7.10 for an ink and wash drawing of Tre'r Ceiri on the Llŷn Peninsula.
Today, original work by Sir Kyffin sells for tens of thousands of pounds.
Bevan added: "The library saw the potential of this young artist.
"It was really important that we were encouraging and supporting young artists at the beginning of their careers, when Kyffin was trying to establish himself as a professional artist."
When he died in September 2006, he left a substantial part of his estate to the library, more than 1,200 works on paper, about 200 oil paintings, more than 300 original prints and his personal archive.
The national library holds the largest collection of Sir Kyffin's work in the world.
Morfudd Bevan said the national library has a long relationship with Sir Kyffin Williams - it bought two pieces from him for £22 at the start of his career
The library hopes the new attraction will introduce more people to his work.
Director of experience Carys Ifan said: "It's by no means a traditional exhibition.
"You go on a journey, literally moving through three rooms that used to be old offices. They've been repurposed because we are so keen to open up more and more to the public."
Profiad Kyffin Experience was made possible by technology invented by Focal Studios, an immersive experience company and the main designers of the exhibition.
Chief executive Dennis Outten said working on the project had been a "labour of love" and an "incredible journey for everyone involved".
In the first room Sir Bryn Terfel tells the story of Sir Kyffin's life in a biligual narration while images taken from his work are projected on to the walls
Focal Studios worked with another company, leo&hyde, to animate Sir Kyffin's paintings in a 360-degree immersive experience so they come alive in projections on the walls and floor.
"It's like you're in one of his paintings, I love it," Outten said.
"It's not like virtual reality, because you can hold the hand of your child, you can sit there with your grandmother or your friend and you experience it together. I think that's incredibly powerful."
Inside the "projection cave", visitors see scenes painted by Sir Kyffin come alive as the cattle, waterfalls, the farmer and his sheepdog move around them.
Outten said high fidelity scans of Sir Kyffin's original work and creative techniques helped bring the paintings to life.
"We actually created a 3D model of Kyffin's farmer and dog, and then using animation techniques, puppeteering them essentially to move."
Rhodri Llwyd Morgan, the library's chief executive, said the new experience was part of a strategy "to be more popular, more appealing and that's our aim".
The experience was formally launched on Thursday and opens to the public from 18 November

Cüzdandaki banknotlara yakından bakınca her birinde harf ve rakamlardan oluşan kendine özgü bir numara olduğunu fark edersiniz. Türkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankası bu seri ve sıra numaralarını banknotun arka yüzüne biri siyah, biri kırmızı mürekkeple iki kez basıyor. Büyüteçle okunabilen minik yazılar ve ışıkta beliren rakamlar da sahteciliğe karşı alınan önlemlerden.
Orijinal banknotların arka yüzünde siyah ve kırmızı mürekkeple basılmış iki seri numarası bulunuyor. Morötesi ışıkta siyah numara yeşil, kırmızı numara kırmızı parlıyor. Sahte paralarda siyah numara yeşil parlamıyor, kırmızıdaki parlama ise bazen taklit ediliyor.
Seri numarasının ön ve arka yüzde ayrı ayrı durduğu sık söylenir ama dolaşımdaki banknotlarda iki numara da arka yüzde. Numarası sayesinde her banknot ötekilerden ayırt edilebiliyor.
Numaralar, Banknot Matbaasında kağıt tabakalarına tasarımla birlikte basılıyor. Tabakalar kesilip kupür haline getiriliyor, makineler her banknotu tek tek inceliyor ve kusurlu olanlar imha ediliyor. TCMB , kendi matbaasında para basan sayılı merkez bankasından biri.
Koleksiyoncular, seri numarası baştan ve sondan okunduğunda aynı kalan banknotlara radar para diyor. Böyle banknotlar yüzündeki değerin üstünde satılabiliyor, resmi değerleri ise üzerinde yazan tutar kadar.
Ön yüzdeki ay yıldızın içinde, kupür değerini gösteren mikro yazılar var. Çıplak gözle seçilemeyen yazılar büyüteçle okunuyor, sahtelerde ise baskı bozulduğu için çoğu zaman okunmuyor.
Banknot ışığa tutulunca beyaz alanda Atatürk portresi ve kupür değerinden oluşan bir filigran beliriyor. Bazı sahtelerde filigran hiç yok, bazılarında baskıyla taklit ediliyor. Ön yüzdeki bazı yazı ve rakamlar kabartma basıldığı için parmakla hissediliyor.
Kağıda gömülü emniyet şeridinde de kupür değeri yazıyor, şerit morötesi ışıkta mavi, kırmızı ya da sarı parlıyor. Arka yüzdeki renk değiştiren şerit, floresan rakamlar ve ışığa tutulunca tamamlanan rakam da aynı işi görüyor.
Ceketin sağındaki yedi köşeli rozete göz hizasından yatay bakınca gizli kupür değeri okunuyor. Banknotların boyu da değerle büyüyor, bir üst kupüre geçildikçe uzun kenar 6 milimetre uzuyor.

Shane MacGowan was best known as the frontman of The Pogues, a band that injected rural folk songs with the punk spirit of the 1970s
On the day of Shane MacGowan's funeral , his heartbroken wife found comfort in the same thing that moved and captivated the rest of the world that afternoon - the music that filled a parish church in Nenagh, County Tipperary.
Mundy and Camille O'Sullivan performed Haunted. Nick Cave sang A Rainy Night in Soho. And Glen Hansard and Lisa O'Neil led mourners in a send-off rendition of Fairytale of New York .
"I thought, well, if we just got all the people who were at the funeral on a record, that'd be something pretty special," Victoria Mary Clarke told BBC News NI.
On Friday, three years after her husband's death, that idea came to fruition with the release of 20th Century Paddy.
"It must be wonderful for Shane... I think up in heaven, he's very aware of what's going on," said Clarke.
There are 36 tracks on the new album - all penned by MacGowan - and 40 bands and soloists.
Among those are contributions from two acclaimed Irish artists who have passed away since recording their covers for the album.
Glen Hansard is featured performing Bottle of Smoke, while Moya Brennan provides her interpretation of Mother Mo Chroi.
"I feel love and connection between the artists (on the album) and Shane.
"And also, you know, for me personally, it feels like a lot of love because when somebody sends something nice to Shane, they're sending it to me."
The Pogues frontman died aged 65 at his Dublin home in 2023, following a hospital stay after being diagnosed with encephalitis.
Shane MacGowan and Victoria Mary married in 2018 after several decades as a couple
Victoria was too fair to say who delivered her favourite cover on the album, but she was frank about how she personally benefited from the project.
"It gave me so much pleasure and it gave me so much joy and hope for the future to work on it because it gave me something to do every single day for three years and it got me out of bed and it got me to make new friends."
In the aftermath of her husband's death, that "social life and a sense of purpose" was invaluable to her.
But while the album is certainly bound up with MacGowan's death, it's not overshadowed by it.
"I think the artwork, if I had to pick, might be my favourite thing about the album," she chirped, an artist herself.
Bruce Springsteen spent time with Shane MacGowan at his home before his death
The term a 'who's who' doesn't quite capture the calibre and genre-defying diversity of the line-up featured on 20th Century Paddy.
There are hall-of-famers like Bruce Springsteen and Tom Waits.
Iconic, generation-crossing indie bands like The Jesus and Mary Chain and The Libertines.
And for anyone who needs reminding of how far above its weight Ireland punches when it comes to music, have a look at the back of 20th Century Paddy.
U2, Hozier and Bob Geldof - people with permanent residencies at top of the music industry.
There are stalwarts and custodians of the Irish folk tradition, Damien Dempsey perhaps foremost among them.
And lots of other artists, less established but very much in their ascendancy - Amble, Kingfishr and Madra Salach, to name but a few.
David Keenan said Shane MacGowan serves as an example of the importance of authenticity in art
David Keenan, a singer-songwriter from Dundalk, whose thoughtful lyrics and intense live performances invoke something of MacGowan himself, told BBC News NI he was honoured to be asked to add to the album.
"Fairytale of New York is as old as Christmas for me," said David.
But his epiphany moment came when an uncle gave him The Pogues' third album.
At 11 years old, Keenan said If I Should Fall from Grace with God "lit a flame" inside him.
"That (album) was the first time I heard all these references to mythology and drink and rebellion and, you know, heartache.
"It gave me permission as a kid to get stuck into real lyric writing. And to do it in the traditional and folk form."
On 20th Century Paddy, Keenan covered Sick Bed of Cúchulainn - a celtic punk ballad from their 1985 album Rum Sodomy and the Lash, the central allusion of which is the mythical Irish warrior Cúchulainn.
This has real significance for Keenan, who as a child in Louth used to play near the standing stone (Clochafarmore) where Cuchulainn was said to have been killed.
He did his recording of the song in Drumlish, County Longford, where he said "Shane used to record too".
"It was just was surreal and at the same time perfect, you know."
Before putting his version down on tape, Keenan did something few artists would have done: he recited a poem he had written in Irish asking permission from MacGowan to sing the song.
"I felt connected to Shane's energy during the recording, you know."
Keenan said the quality of the artists on 20th Century Paddy showed the "global respect that was there for Shane's abilities, you know, as a lyric writer, a poet".
He added that, at a time when there is "a lot of pressure on young musicians now to go viral on TikTok and dumb themselves down... here's an artist who didn't do that".
"In an age of ChatGPT and generative AI", said Keenan, MacGowan is a reminder for "human beings to be authentic".
Keenan's top picks from the album included Summer in Siam covered by Tom Waits, Jimmy Artache's version of USA, Glenn Hansard's Bottle of Smoke and Steve Earle's If I Should Fall From Grace With God.
But, given the quality on the album, the list, he said, could have gone on... and on... and on.

Mario Frick has been announced as the new head coach of Aberdeen, taking over from the sacked Stephen Robinson to become the club's fourth manager in 2026.
Capped 125 times as a striker for Liechtenstein, the 52-year-old was last in charge at Luzern, leaving the Swiss club in the summer after five years.
He follows Robinson, Peter Leven and Jimmy Thelin in leading the side in this calendar year and will take charge for the first time against Scottish Premiership bottom side Kilmarnock on Saturday.
"Throughout our discussions, he demonstrated a clear vision, strong leadership qualities and a deep understanding of what is required to build a successful team," said Pittodrie chief executive Adrian Bevington.
"He was also exceptionally well regarded by the many people across the game we consulted during the process, and the board was unanimous in its belief that he is the right person to lead Aberdeen forward."
Former Motherwell and St Mirren boss Robinson was dismissed on 9 November, with Aberdeen second bottom of the Scottish Premiership, having lost four games in a row.
'Aberdeen hunt yet another manager after ill-fated Robinson reign'
Watch new Aberdeen boss Frick score against Scotland in September 2010
Frick, who also managed Vaduz in the Swiss Super League, will be assisted by Roman Matter and is the seventh permanent manager since Dave Cormack took control of the club in November 2019.
As a player, his former clubs include FC Basel, FC Zurich, St. Gallen and Grasshopper, while his 16 international goals make him Liechtenstein's all-time top scorer.
"Mario is a strong personality with clear ideas about how he wants his teams to play," added sporting director Lutz Pfannenstiel. "He brings energy, ambition and a winning mentality, and knows how to build a strong team environment.
"We were looking for the right person to lead the next chapter of Aberdeen FC, and I'm convinced Mario has the qualities, character and vision to make a real impact."
Frick got Vaduz promoted in 2020 before helping Luzern avoid relegation following his move there in 2021.
The next again year he guided them to a fourth-placed finish and European qualification, although they were knocked out of Conference League qualifying by Lee Johnson's Hibernian.
Aberdeen say Frick "has built a strong reputation for transforming teams, handing top-flight debuts to more than 30 academy players during his coaching career".
Hibs striker Thibault Klidje and current Aberdeen goalkeeper Marius Muller both played under him.
Aberdeen did not disclose contract details for Frick as he takes over a side with just three wins from 12 Premiership outings this season.
One of his international goals came at Hampden Park in 2010 when a late Stephen McManus header rescued a 2-1 win for Scotland.

Arsenal and London City Lionesses played out an entertaining 1-1 draw but the result did little to bolster European qualification hopes for Renée Slegers’s side as the visitors’ goalkeeper Mary Earps produced a fine display to thwart the north London side.
Frida Maanum finished off a superb team move for Arsenal to open the scoring early on but her goal was quickly cancelled out by a terrific finish from Isobel Goodwin and Arsenal eventually had to settle for their fifth draw in 10 Women’s Super League matches this season.
Arsenal had secured an impressive result in Barcelona on Thursday, drawing with the European champions, but this game against the WSL’s third-placed side felt as though it was of even greater importance, particularly if Arsenal wish to continue visiting venues such as Camp Nou next season.
Just like they had done away at Anfield last weekend, Renée Slegers’ team made a very bright start with energy, pace and the threat of Alessia Russo. Emily Fox’s shot was deflected wide, after a good move that included some excellent Maanum build-up play, before Ona Batlle’s long-range effort bounced just wide. It was not long before Maanum tucked in the opening goal after an intelligent cutback from Russo.
The visitors struck back almost immediately, though, as Goodwin did superbly to turn inside Leah Williamson, inside the penalty area, and then demonstrated the strength and composure to hold off Lisa Baum and fire a lethal finish past Misa Rodríguez with power and precision. It was a timely moment of class from the English striker in front of the watching gaze of the England head coach, Sarina Wiegman, who was in the stands ahead of naming her next England squad on Tuesday morning.
Viviane Asseyi scored twice as West Ham secured back-to-back WSL home wins after beating rock-bottom Charlton 2-0.
Asseyi’s curled finish put the Irons in front just ahead of the break and she then scored a 25-yard free-kick early in the second half. The defeat saw Charlton, who remain without a point, become the first WSL team to lose all 10 of their opening matches of the season.
Hathilde Harviken’s late goal gave Aston Villa a 1-0 win over derby rivals Birmingham , which gives Brian Sørensen his third win since stepping in as interim manager and leaves his side seventh. Press Association
Earps then saved well from Baum to keep the scores level at half-time, but her finest saves were still to follow after the break.
In the second half, after a brief spell of Arsenal endeavour which saw Earps do well to dive low to her left to divert a Caitlin Foord strike wide, what followed was a sustained spell of London City possession, territory and chances. Eder Maestre’s team spent a good part of 20 minutes firmly camped in Arsenal’s half and they carved open a good chance for Kadidiatou Diani but her relatively tame, low, near-post effort was saved by Rodríguez.
Diani’s 62nd-minute replacement from the substitutes’ bench, Delphine Cascarino, drew gasps from the crowd as she unleashed a dipping strike that bounced off the top of the crossbar. It was a lucky escape for Arsenal, who were seeing an alarming lack of the ball.
Arsenal, who had won all seven of their previous meetings with London City across all competitions, were then denied by two more fine Earps stops, firstly from a Maanum close-range effort and then from Maanum’s hgh curler, which had looked destined for the top corner before Earps touched it on to the bar.
Slegers’s 50th WSL match in charge of the north London side almost ended in defeat late on but Alexia Putellas’s rising, stoppage-time strike flew narrowly over the bar.

Selahattin Paşalı ile Lara Paşalı'nın boşanacağı yönündeki iddialar, çiftin özel hayatına ilişkin gündeme gelen haberlerin ardından konuşulmaya başlandı. Daha önce evliliklerinde sorunlar yaşadığı ve ilişkilerine yeniden şans verdiği öne sürülen çiftin bu kez ayrılık kararı aldığı iddia edildi.

Izzy Goodwin scored from her one shot on target against Arsenal
After 10 games in the Women's Super League season, London City Lionesses have shown they are capable of finishing inside the top three.
Their narrow 2-1 defeat by Manchester City two weeks ago provided snippets of their potential but a 1-1 draw at the Emirates against an improved Arsenal on Sunday confirmed their credentials.
Eder Maestre's side sit third in the table - the last qualification spot for next season's Women's Champions League - and are six points above Arsenal.
It is a strong position to be in just shy of the halfway stage having already faced big hitters Arsenal, Manchester City and Manchester United.
Current leaders Chelsea await in December but, for now, London City's progress is moving at a pace that looks set to challenge the usual suspects.
Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed
Goodwin's glorious solo strike draws London City Lionesses level
A sold-out away end helped fill out the 32,000-strong crowd at the Emirates on Sunday as many hoped for an end-to-end encounter.
They were not disappointed as fearless London City showed bravery against an Arsenal side who played with a spark following their 1-1 draw with Barcelona.
The visitors were helped out by Arsenal's wastefulness - the Gunners had 17 shots and only converted one - but London City caused plenty of problems of their own.
Maestre said after their defeat by Manchester City that their opponents showed more experience and know-how but against Arsenal, his side matured.
They were under pressure early on and fell a goal down thanks to Frida Maanum's opener but it took just 98 seconds for Izzy Goodwin to equalise for London City.
That killed Arsenal's momentum and when the pressure increased again from the hosts in the second half, goalkeeper and player of the match Mary Earps stepped up to make crucial saves.
"The performance was there. We had the chances to score and get a better result but Arsenal had chances too. The game was very open," said Maestre.
"The way we faced and challenged every circumstance in the game shows we are here, and able to play with that mentality in these big games.
"We came here to take risks. Our energy was good. We were brave and weren't scared about the context or the opponent.
"We tried to play as if we were at home. I always want to feel that my teams are brave and go for the win."
That bravery showed as Alexia Putellas came close twice with long-range efforts, Goodwin could have been onside when she was played in behind later on.
London City hit the crossbar through substitute Delphine Cascarino and had 14 shots compared to Arsenal's 17, including four inside the box.
Arsenal are still yet to win at home this season in the WSL but this was still an impressive showing from London City, who came to the Emirates to play.
But while they were willing to take risks, they were smarter than they were against Manchester City, choosing when to press aggressively and when to hold off.
"We tried to match the pace of the ball and not expose ourselves as much to the players that Arsenal have," added Maestre.
"We were trying to mix the moments we were more clinical in our press. We made some adjustments at half-time and were much better at recognising those."
London City are backed by US billionaire Michele Kang and that has made a big difference in the transfer market.
They recruited superstars Alexia Putellas, Mary Earps, Mapi Leon and Kadidiatou Diani in the summer.
Such is their depth that high-flying Spaniard Lucia Corrales, the dangerous Cascarino and England international Freya Godfrey came off the bench.
Those individual talents have made a difference and on Sunday it was goalkeeper Earps who took the plaudits, claiming the player of the match award.
She made crucial saves late on as Arsenal pushed ferociously for a winner, tipping Maanum's effort onto the crossbar and blocking her shot from close range.
Earps had to bide her time for the number one shirt after making the switch from Paris St-Germain this summer but has started the past three WSL games.
"Mary is a very strong character and is much more than the things we see in terms of the performance," said Maestre.
"She has experience, and energy that you can bring to every part in the process and not just the things we see in the matches.
"I think the energy that she brings to the position is massive and has a massive impact. I'm very pleased with her."
Watching on in the stands was England boss Sarina Wiegman who will have been pleased with the display from goalscorer Goodwin.
The 23-year-old got the better of England captain Leah Williamson when she fooled her with quick feet and fired the ball into the back of the net, making it 1-1.
She is proof that competition for places in the London City starting XI is pushing players on and that their depth is improving each week.
"I think Izzy is becoming a more mature player. She has the inner competition and the signings sometimes push you to bring 100% every time," added Maestre.
"She is committed to keep pushing and, with the performances she is having, why not [earn an England call-up]?
"Izzy is moving forward in the ways she can take advantage and that commitment is the way she is reaching those performances. I'm very proud of her."

A football tournament for nine and 10 year olds in Bergamo, Italy, was abandoned because of the behaviour of parents, which included fighting and shouting homophobic insults towards a child and a referee.
The tournament was arranged by Serie D club Villa Valle, and Italian news agency Ansa reported , external that the referees used were young people involved at the club.
Organisers of the event and the coaches of all teams involved agreed to suspend the tournament during the final match of the day because of the parents' quarrels which also included spitting and booing opposing teams.
Villa Valle posted a statement on social media, condemning the behaviour which they described as "painful to witness", but also praised the attitudes of the children playing and their coaches.
"Villa Valle wishes to express its strongest condemnation of the disrespectful and violent behaviour displayed by some parents in the stands," the club said.
"With deep disappointment, our club found itself compelled to take a decision that was as difficult as it was necessary: to bring the final match of the tournament to an early end and to suspend the awards ceremony, in order to send a strong and unequivocal message against attitudes that have nothing whatsoever to do with the values of sport.
"After a day characterised by matches played in a spirit of fairness, mutual respect and sportsmanship by the young athletes and coaching staff, it was particularly painful to witness such deplorable incidents in the stands.
"We strongly believe in the educational value of sport, especially at youth level, and we are convinced that adults should serve as positive role models for young people, not become the protagonists of behaviour that risks undermining the true meaning of these events."

41 min Cucurella and Bellingham contest a 50-50, the ball landing perfectly to Anderson, who controls a terrific long, low pass, curving around the outside of the Spain block for Kane. He knows he’s not got the pace to do Cubarsi on the outside, so he holds then explodes on the inside and Cubarsi’s challenge is lazy, taking man and nothing else.
40 min Baena picks up the ball just outside the box and picks a lovely pass, punched straight and in behind for Lamine … but Hall, who’s enjoying himself, stretches to intercept. England have defended really well so far.
39 min Hall crosses from the left and Belling ham is up on the far side, but can’t wrap his head around enough of the ball to knock it back across and Simon gathers.
38 min “Lenny Walker’s decision to bring on Dale Banton for Aldershot (as was then) late on against Halfax at The Rec in, ooh, 1990(?) was pretty dreadful,” reckons David Johnson. “Fluffed a load of chances. 36 min Again, England jump on Zubimendi, Gordon at him and finding Rogers, who flips a square pass towards the back post, but Laporte does enough to flick away. 35 min “1970 World Cup quarter final, England v West Germany,” says Rhys Davies. “Ramsey took off Bobby Charlton, freeing up Beckenbauer. The rest is history.”
Yup, that might be the daddy – Norman Hunter for Martin Peters was also a vibe.
34 min England win a free-kick down the right, Rice coming from behind it to generate the chwhip he’s after … only to overhit, Simon coming to claim.
31 min Kane drops deep and accepts the ball on the back foot, under pressure … and Ruiz robs him, but England quickly win it back. They look really well organised in terms of defensive structure but, more than that, there’s a desire from each individual to take responsibility. The question, though, is whether they can keep that focus and discipline across 90 minutes, and whether their attackers can create; it’s been a while since they exerted serious pressure on the Spain defence.
30 min It’s a bit messy now, which England won’t mind. They’re set up for a physical contest, and the more play is broken, the more they’re able to enforce that advantage.
28 min Tuchel’s performance against Argentina is surely one of the great managerial eff-ups; which others spring to mind? Those in my head: Pep Guardiola, Man City v Chelsea in the 2021 Champions League final; Alex Ferguson, Man United v Chelsea 2010. Any more for any more?
26 min Cucurella and Baena combine down the left and Ruiz’s subsequent cross is a goodun, but Quansah does really well to head clear, the ball landing on Porro’s laces … and ensuing volley landing I don’t even know where.
25 min Simon takes a liberty, drilling a hopeful pass through the middle of the pitch to which Konsa is first. He meets the ball with a solid header, finding Bellingham, who I think is offside, and once the shot slides by the near post, the flag is raised.
23 min We’re into that 4-4-2-block stage, Spain pinning them back into their shape, and Lamine slipping a pass into Baena, through the legs of Barcelona teammate Gordon; I doubt this is the last he’ll hear of a shameful episode.
22 min Lamine runs at Hall, who maybe just about fouls him. The requested yellow card does not follow, and the free-kick eludes Porro.
21 min Yup, Pedro Porro replaces Pubill – a change I think may actually help Spain , the new man’s first-phase excellence, ability to invert and goal-threat of greater use than the physicality they’re losing.
19 min Pubill is hurt, clattered by Simon when the keeper came to punch that second England corner; I don’t think he can carry on.
18 min And here comes Hall, picking a diag that takes him from touchline to box, beating two men with Rogers bumrushing the near post. The cross, though, is blocked behind then, when the corner comes in, another inswinging brute from Rice, Kane heads past the far post. He’ll be relieved the flag goes up, for that was a chance.
17 min The game has settled after that rabid England start, Spain much more of a factor now, but here come England again, Anderson megging Merino and Kane moving the ball on. Nothing comes of it, but England step on to them again!
15 min The free-kick is swung out, but Oyarzabal can’t get enough on it and Quansah, who’s started well, imparts enough of a touch to see it away.
15 min The first flash of Lamine, who runs at Hall, moves inside via nutmeg – ouch – then Rice clips him from behind and is booked.
14 min Already, the inclusion of Merino is giving Spain a problem – when he drops, Quansah is following him, and he’s not able to make the extra man in midfield.
13 min So far, England have had 62% possession. Do not adjust your television sets, this is not a misprint.
11 min England’s press is excellent, its latest application forcing Simon to kick long; Wimblespain! Of course, at some point, the pass-and-move is likely to assume control, but if Tuchel’s men can grab a goal, they’ve the ability on the counter to add to it.
9 min This is the best nine minutes England have played under Tuchel and probably Southgate too, bristling with confidence, intensity and menace. Gordon gets Pubill squared, barges by on the outside … but his cut-back is into traffic.

3 min Gosh, am I dreaming? England win the ball high with Rice, securing a second corner … and this time, Simon comes to punch clear.

Tremendous start from England, but might they already regret these missed opportunities?

Anthem time, the pashun side-contest won convincingly by Rice.

One hallmark of Mauricio Pochettino’s time in international management was been his refusal to embrace the term “friendly.” His preferred branding is “unofficial games”.
His spin gained a bit of validity on Saturday, in the New York Red Bulls’ “friendly” against Club América, marred by a mass brawl between the sides that resulted in five red cards and a bevy of beverages thrown from the stands.
The game itself was odd for a few reasons. First, the Red Bulls have already been eliminated from MLS’s comically forgiving postseason, which means players (aside from veterans like Emil Forsberg) delayed vacations for a glorified scrimmage. Second, the match was announced on 1 October, at which point it was abundantly clear that the NWSL’s Gotham FC, a tenant of the Red Bulls’ Sports Illustrated Stadium, could host a playoff semi-final on the same weekend.
That scheduling snafu, combined with the comically poor state of the pitch, became a serious problem for the NWSL club, who settled for 5,000-seat Icahn Stadium for Sunday’s semi-final.
For the Red Bulls, the show must go on – and boy, did they find a way to entertain the fans who showed up for the low-stakes affair.
Not with their soccer exploits, mind you. Playing without the aforementioned veterans and US internationals Julian Hall and Adri Mehmeti, the remaining Red Bulls came ready for a scrap. At one point in the second half, América goalkeeper Rodolfo Cota required treatment for taking a boot above his knee while closing a shooting angle, putting the visitors on alert.
Roughly 40 minutes into the second half, this unofficial game abandoned any attempt to be friendly. Mijahir Jiménez dribbled toward the right corner flag, only to be taken down by a defender. He took great umbrage to the nature of the challenge, kicking off a maelstrom of shoves, punches, thrown drinks from the crowd, and men pressing their chests and foreheads together like bighorn rams in the throes of the rutting season.
The full sequence lives on thanks to a live watch-along streamed on YouTube, where former Mexico defender Miguel Layún comes to life in his gamer chair and begs his compatriots to keep the fracas alive. The fracas lasted 65 seconds, while the ensuing corner kick came a full seven minutes after Jimenez’s dribble.
The only scoreline from the night that matters: three Red Bulls sent off, three players from América, with the final five minutes being an eight-v-eight affair. The referee decided to forego any second half stoppage time, almost certainly for the best.

Arsenal Women vs London City Lionesses. Barclays Women's Super League.
Report and free match highlights as Arsenal's wait for a home WSL win goes on after a 1-1 draw against London City Lionesses; the Gunners have now drawn all five games at the Emirates this season; Frida Maanum's early strike was immediately cancelled out by Izzy Goodwin
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Arsenal's wait for a home WSL win continues as they drew 1-1 against London City Lionesses on Sunday - their fifth draw in a row at the Emirates this season - with an inspired Mary Earps denying the Gunners victory.
While the result extends Arsenal's unbeaten home run to 24 league matches, it is becoming an increasing concern and a spectre on the shoulder that the Gunners have been unable to secure three points at the Emirates this year.
Giving her view to Sky Sports after the game, Renee Slegers - managing her 50th Arsenal game - said: "We spent more time than we normally do without the ball; partly the game plan and partly them asking questions of us on the pitch.
"We create big chances, could have done more with those. That's the frustrating part. This is the fifth [home game] and we couldn't give the fans the win. Unfortunately we couldn't do it for them."
It was two early goals that decided the fixture too. Frida Maanum scored for a second game in a row - having netted against Barcelona in the Champions League in midweek - slotting home from an Alessia Russo cross to put Arsenal ahead.
But a minute later, London City were level. Leah Williamson lost the run of the lively Izzy Goodwin, and the striker lashed into the roof of the net.
From then on, it was a goalkeeping masterclass from former England No 1 Earps especially that kept Arsenal from scoring another with her counterpart Misa Rodriguez also making her fair share of saves, albeit not as frequently.
The Gunners simply could not find a way past the inspired London City stopper as Lionesses boss Sarina Wiegman watched on from the stands.
The pick of her string of world-class saves came when she tipped a Maanum shot onto the crossbar. It came shortly after substitute Delphine Cascarino had also rattled the woodwork at the other end.
The result does little to improve either side's WSL standings, and Arsenal's hopes of finishing in the Champions League places takes another hit. They are sixth on 14 points - already six behind London City in third.
"We were happy with the one point, we wanted and needed three today," Slegers added. "Every game is three points for Arsenal when we play for this club.
"At the moment, with our position in the table and how we need to stay connected and compete for the top three positions for the Champions League, this one was very important for us.
"With that being said, the season isn't over. It's still November and we have to look at what it looks like in May."
10: GOAL! A sweeping move is finished by Maanum after Russo's cutback to give Arsenal the lead.
11: GOAL! London City immediately equalise as Goodwin fires into the roof of the net.
22: SAVE! Earps makes a good stop to deny Lisa Baum, who cuts in from the right-hand side.
27: SAVE! Misa Rodriguez on hand this time to deny Alexia Putellas.
29: SAVE! Again from Earps! This time it's a flying effort to keep out another Baum shot.
68: CROSSBAR! Cascarino pings an effort off the top of the woodwork.
77: DOUBLE SAVE! Earps pulls off another brilliant double save, first to deny Smith then Maanum.
85: CROSSBAR! Earps fingertips a Maanum shot onto the crossbar.
Before Sunday's game, S ky Sports asked whether Arsenal have lost their fear factor at the Emirates this season.
The answer surely has to be yes - although after the game, Slegers was adamant that the fear factor has not gone, despite being without a win.
Teams have come to the Emirates and sat in a low block that the Gunners have been unable to break down more than once.
London City were never going to do that. It's not in their DNA. They closer resemble the Barcelona team Arsenal faced on Thursday where, funnily enough, they drew 1-1.
But what they might not have been banking on was an ingenious performance from Earps. While Arsenal did not have to worry about defenders sitting back, they did face a goalkeeper putting in one of the performances of the season. How's your luck?
She made eight saves as Arsenal continued to pepper her goal - her most in the WSL since 2017 - and the second-most in the WSL this season after the goalkeeper that replaces her at Man Utd, Phallon Tullis-Joyce.
When asked how she found the game, Earps told Sky Sports: "Tiring. It's a big point away from home.
"Either team could have won it in terms of chances. Happy with the point - would have liked three. All the girls put their bodies on the line. I love defending. It was tough today and I thought we did a good job."
It was perhaps made all the sweeter for her that her former England boss Sarina Wiegman was watching on. It is well-documented how she departed the national team, but it certainly showed the Lionesses head coach what she was missing.
Earps has had to bide her time at London City, with Elene Lete continuing to be the No 1 until recently. The former England No 1 has now started in three games, and while she is yet to keep a clean sheet, she will have staked a huge claim to the permeant spot with her performance on Sunday.
